newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Committee urged to decide Israel monetary policy.
newsitem.headline: Committee urged to decide Israel monetary policy.

text.p: An internal panel set up by Bank of Israel Governor Jacob Frenkel has recommended that monetary policy should be decided by a committee of economists and central bank officials headed by Frenkel.

The internal panel, headed by former deputy central bank governor Zvi Zussman, was set up a year ago by Frenkel after consultation with late prime minister Yitzhak Rabin to study the structure of the central bank, its aims and policies. This came amid public pressure to curb the governor's power and prevent him from making decisions alone on interest rates.
Currently an advisory committee discusses monetary policy with the governor but the final decision is Frenkel's alone.

Industry leaders, former finance minister Abraham Shohat and other economic bodies in Israel had called for the setting up of a committee that would include representatives from the business sector to determine interest rate policy.

The Zussman committee has called for the creation of a committee that would include prominent economic figures and central bank officials but would exclude government officials, industrialists and bankers who have their own vested interests, a central bank spokesman said.
Such a committee would help maintain the central bank's independence.
The committee said it was necessary to specifically define the aims of the central bank and give it adequate instruments to implement its policies.
The central bank spokesman said Frenkel will give feedback on the report and a final version then will be presented to Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
